text:
kevin: heads up — ran into a weird abort/cancel interaction across SDKs while testing streaming on mobile + rust bridge. not blocking prod but weird duplicates on retry.

maya: rough tl;dr? can you repro consistently?

kevin: yes, repro steps quick: start a streaming generate, call AbortController.abort() in node client (we mirror same behavior in mobile), client sees stream end, then client retry kicks in and server emits remaining tokens again — duplicates.

kevin: code snippet (node):
```js
const ac = new AbortController();
const res = await client.stream.generate({prompt}, {signal: ac.signal});
// user cancels
ac.abort();
```

ben: does the server get any explicit CANCEL frame or just TCP close? on mobile we sometimes get a graceful close vs abrupt.

kevin: for node it closes the response stream (client side) but underlying connection often stays open. mobile -> native bridge sends a CANCEL event but we don't surface a special header. server treats it as client disconnect; runtime may keep processing until checkpoint then emit.

maya: possible root causes: 1) abort semantics differ across transports (fetch vs okhttp vs rust async), 2) our retry logic is trigger-happy (retries on any non-200 or early EOF), 3) no idempotency key so server can't dedupe partial outputs.

sarah: agree — quick mitigation: make streaming retry opt-in and add request_id header for dedupe. also add a short debounce (200ms) before retrying so transient aborts settle.

ben: i'll open a tiny opt-in flag PR for mobile/rust to disable auto-retry during streaming. linking: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1234

ci-bot: build passed for PR #1234 (:white_check_mark:)

kevin: nice. long term i think SDKs should send an explicit "client_cancelled" event over the stream before closing so server can short-circuit rather than finish. protocol change but much cleaner for cost and duplicate avoidance.

maya: agreed. can we add an experiment: send client_cancelled and server to respond with 499 or special final frame, not a retryable closure?

ben: yeah we'll sketch API proposal in the PR description and include test matrix for node/python/mobile/rust.

kevin: also small interop note — python contextlib cancel currently raises RuntimeError in some cases; we'll unify to throw CancelledError (align with asyncio.CancelledError) so higher-level retry logic can detect cancellation vs transient failure.

maya: pinging @sarah for a quick review on the node streaming teardown tests — should be small.

sarah: on it, will review within the hour :coffee: 

kevin: thanks. leaving a checklist: [ ] disable streaming auto-retry (opt-in) [ ] add request_id header for dedupe [ ] propose client_cancelled frame + server 499 handling [ ] unify python exception type.

ben: sounds good. i'll update PR and add mobile test harness.

ci-bot: added to pipeline: interop-tests/streaming/cancel-suite
